To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of a video based learning environment in the context of a teaching practicum did not lead to a significant improvement of self efficacy beliefs, knowledge of inclusive education or attitudes towards inclusion.
the online and video based peer feedback learning environment did not improve the preservice teachers' self efficacy, attitudes towards inclusion, and knowledge of inclusive practices.

the online and video based peer feedback learning environment was effective in increasing pre service teachers self efficacy beliefs in handling classroom disruptions and their knowledge of inclusion.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the effects of a video and online based learning environment on the self efficacy beliefs, the attitudes and the knowledge of pre service teachers regarding inclusion during a teaching practicum in inclusive classrooms.
the effects of a video based peer feedback on preservice teachers' self efficacy, their knowledge of inclusive and their attitudes towards inclusion.
the impact of an onlinenetwork on pre service teachers self efficacy beliefs and knowledge of inclusive classrooms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

there are no significant differences in the effects of the online and video based intervention on pre service teachers self efficacy beliefs and knowledge of inclusive practices compared to a traditional teaching practicum.
there are no differences between students who received the online based learning environment and students who received conventional supervision.

the use of online and video based feedback did not lead to an improvement of self efficacy beliefs, knowledge of inclusive education and attitudes towards inclusion of pre service teachers during their teaching practicum.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
pre service teachers are able to learn from video based peer feedback in an online learning environment.
the online and video based environment did not have a significant impact on preservice teachers attitudes towards inclusion or self efficacy beliefs.
the online and video based environment is a promising way to improve preservice teachers self-efficacy and knowledge of inclusive teaching.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pre service teachers can learn a lot about inclusive education from a practicum.
online and video based feedback in combination with conventional practicum supervision can be a useful addition to the training of preservice teachers.
the development of self efficacy beliefs and the improvement of attitudes towards inclusion and the knowledge of inclusive education is possible.
